title: A triangle-free strongly regular graph on 162 vertices
credit: Classical question (Biggs, Brouwer); smallest open case per A. E. Brouwer's table of strongly regular graphs.
premise_risks: Same family as the pending degree-57 Moore graph (H06); scorer may see overlap
AI-assisted SRG exclusions are moving quickly in 2026 (Kovaľ + AI; Akiyama), so this case may fall soon
Pure existence question resolved, if at all, likely by computation
plain: Only seven triangle-free strongly regular graphs are known (pentagon, Petersen, Clebsch, Hoffman-Singleton, Gewirtz, M22 and Higman-Sims graphs). The smallest parameter set for which such a graph is neither known nor ruled out has 162 vertices, every vertex of degree 21, no triangles, and every pair of non-adjacent vertices with exactly 3 common neighbours. Does such a graph exist?
math: Decide whether there exists a simple graph on $162$ vertices that is strongly regular with parameters $(162,21,0,3)$: $21$-regular, adjacent vertices have no common neighbours, and distinct non-adjacent vertices have exactly $3$ common neighbours.
